He says there is a hardening over ethnic Israel until all Gentiles are grafted in, and only then will all of Israel be complete. That hardening is supposed to happen. It is required by Paul's own theology. What he was disagreeing with was not my argument. He was disagreeing with Paul.
He also didn't know why it's called the West Bank. The region sits on the east side of Israel. Jordan, which only declared independence in 1946, two years before Israel, coined the term. It's west of the Jordan River, from Jordan's perspective. I asked him: as a Christian debating this topic, why are you using a political term invented by a country that was two years old?
I asked him what country Jaffa is in. He said Palestine. I reminded him: five minutes ago you told me you call it the West Bank because that's what it's called internationally today. Now you're rejecting the modern name when it's Israel. He said: "From that view, I'll grant you that."
He didn't know Jordan was given 78% of the land called Palestine by the British Mandate. He didn't know Palestine declared independence in 1988 in Algiers, 40 years after Israel. He didn't know the word Palestine was not given by Arabs, not by the indigenous people of any kind, it was named by Roman Emperor Hadrian after the Philistines, invaders from the Aegean most likely from Crete. In Hebrew and ancient Egyptian, Philistine means invader. When you say "I'm from Palestine," you're saying you're from the land of invaders.
